--- title: "Clustering" subtitle: "Neighbourhood Transport Environment Typology" author: "Laurie Platt" date: last-modified date-format: "[Last updated ] DD MMMM, YYYY" format: html: css: resources/styles.css code-tools: true self-contained: false code-fold: true toc: true toc-depth: 5 toc-expand: 1 number-sections: true fig-cap-location: top fig-align: left code-links: - text: scc-pi/transport-env-typology icon: github href: https://github.com/scc-pi/transport-env-typology execute: warning: false message: false cache: false --- # Introduction ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Packages library(tidyverse) library(here) library(targets) library(gt) library(gtExtras) library(sf) library(leaflet) library(tidymodels) library(tidyclust) # Sources all R/*.R same as _targets.R tar_source() # Objects needed from our {targets} pipeline tar_load(df_lsoa) # ggplot theme set_theme(theme_minimal()) ``` ::: Having acquired our data ([ETL](etl.qmd)) and spent some time understanding it ([EDA](eda.qmd)), this page will employ clustering algorithms. We're using the {tidymodels}^[{tidymodels} R packages ([www.tidymodels.org](https://www.tidymodels.org/))] framework, a collection of R packages for machine learning. In particular, we're using the {tidyclust}^[{tidyclust} R package ([tidyclust.tidymodels.org](https://tidyclust.tidymodels.org/index.html))] R package, which is effectively a clustering specific replacement for the {tidymodels} package {parsnip}^[{parsnip} R package ([parsnip.tidymodels.org](https://parsnip.tidymodels.org/))]. ```{mermaid} %%| label: fig-overview %%| echo: true %%| code-fold: true %%| fig-cap: Code overview flowchart TD df["data
df_lsoa"] rec["recipe
lsoa_rec"] spec["specification
kmeans_spec"] wf["workflow

kmeans_fit"] aug["augment

LSOA21CD + cluster"] rec --> wf spec --> wf df --> fit wf --> fit fit --> aug fit --> cent fit --> eval df --> eval df --> clust aug --> clust ``` # Data Data frame `df_lsoa` has 33 candidate variables for clustering. Notes on the production of `df_lsoa` are in the [ETL page](etl.qmd). Below is a sample of candidate variables. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df_lsoa |> select(1, 2, 3, 15, 25, 30) |> glimpse() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Rows: 343 Columns: 6 $ LSOA21CD "E01007823", "E01007824", "E01007825", "E01007826", … $ area_km2 0.4213668, 0.3453409, 1.2641171, 1.0513878, 1.541163… $ road_length_m 7066.935, 4043.432, 7752.928, 4833.948, 8113.129, 48… $ pct_30mph_or_less 0.8571429, 1.0000000, 0.8365385, 1.0000000, 1.000000… $ imd_decile 4, 10, 10, 10, 8, 6, 7, 6, 7, 8, 7, 7, 6, 7, 6, 8, 9… $ hh_no_car 181, 59, 91, 52, 151, 169, 175, 158, 144, 141, 188, … ``` ::: ::: # Recipe Our recipe^[{recipes} R package ([recipes.tidymodels.org](https://recipes.tidymodels.org/))]: 1. Specifies the key i.e. `LSOA21CD`. 1. Removes selected variables e.g. `cycle_infra_length_m`. 1. Normalises numeric data. Some notes on selecting and transforming candidate variables are in the [EDA page](eda.qmd) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} # LSOA21CD is kept as an ID so it is not used as a clustering predictor lsoa_rec <- recipes::recipe(~ ., data = df_lsoa) |> recipes::update_role(LSOA21CD, new_role = "id") |> recipes::step_rm( starts_with("cycle_infra_"), count_point_n, starts_with("mean_aadf_") ) |> recipes::step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) ``` ::: # Specification. Define a model that fits clusters based on distances to a number of centres^[Getting started with tidyclust ([tidyclust.tidymodels.org/articles/tidyclust.html#extract-results](https://tidyclust.tidymodels.org/articles/tidyclust.html#extract-results))]. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} kmeans_spec <- tidyclust::k_means(num_clusters = 6, engine = "stats") kmeans_spec ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` K Means Cluster Specification (partition) Main Arguments: num_clusters = 6 Computational engine: stats ``` ::: ::: # Workflow Create a workflow to "bundle together our pre-processing, modelling, and post-processing requests^[{workflows} R package ([workflows.tidymodels.org](https://workflows.tidymodels.org/))]". ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} kmeans_wf <- workflows::workflow(lsoa_rec, kmeans_spec) kmeans_wf ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ══ Workflow ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Preprocessor: Recipe Model: k_means() ── Preprocessor ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 2 Recipe Steps • step_rm() • step_normalize() ── Model ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── K Means Cluster Specification (partition) Main Arguments: num_clusters = 6 Computational engine: stats ``` ::: ::: # Workflow fitted Fit the workflow to the data. The recipe describes *how* to preprocess the data, but it doesn't contain any data. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} set.seed(1234) kmeans_fit <- tidyclust::fit(kmeans_wf, data = the k-means centres and cluster assignments, so it can label the data it was trained on, but it can't recompute distances from the original observations. The metrics we're going to use need those distances, so they need to take the data as an argument. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tidyclust::sse_within_total(kmeans_fit, df_lsoa) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 3 .metric .estimator .estimate 1 sse_within_total standard 4829. ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} tidyclust::sse_ratio(kmeans_fit, df_lsoa) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 3 .metric .estimator .estimate 1 sse_ratio standard 0.543 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} tidyclust::silhouette_avg(kmeans_fit, df_lsoa) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 3 .metric .estimator .estimate 1 silhouette_avg standard 0.170 ``` ::: :::
